metric.name: startup_ttfd_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.startup.startups;
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.startup.time_to_display;
WITH
  cold AS (
    SELECT s.package, d.time_to_full_display AS ns
    FROM android_startups AS s
    JOIN android_startup_time_to_display AS d USING (startup_id)
    WHERE s.startup_type = 'cold'
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT package FROM cold GROUP BY package ORDER BY count(*) DESC, package LIMIT 1
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT ns, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY ns) AS rank, count(*) OVER () AS n
    FROM cold
    WHERE package = (SELECT package FROM app) AND ns IS NOT NULL
  )
SELECT (SELECT ns / 1e6 FROM ranked WHERE rank = (n + 1) / 2) AS value

claims.text: The startup measurements are for com.superplayer.demo cold starts: the baseline contains 20 startup rows and the current trace contains 20 startup rows, with the current rows showing consistently higher time-to-full-display values.

Commit fb30a9c67862bd42f9d8fab36f6c8dff37069417 registers DemoApplication as the app Application class and adds launch-time catalog-cache rebuilding and checksum work, making it the correlated culprit for the startup regression.

caveats: The captures run on an SDK 36 sdk_gphone64_arm64 emulator, so absolute startup timings may not represent physical devices.
The trace evidence establishes the startup regression and correlates it with the launch-time Application change; it does not directly attribute individual startup samples to a specific Java method.

dropped_claims.text: Median cold-start time to full display increased from 2077.310959 ms in the baseline to 2723.988335 ms in the current trace, a 646.677376 ms regression.
